title: SQL Mission 7: Replace IN Subquery With JOINed Aggregate

-- Find customers with more than 5 orders.
-- Use a joined aggregate instead of IN (subquery).
--
-- Rules:
--   1. Aggregate orders in a subquery
--   2. Use HAVING to filter groups
--   3. Join back to customers for names
--
-- Tables:
--   customers(customer_id, name, email, region)
--   orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, status, total_amount)

SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  c.name,
  -- TODO: total_orders from subquery
FROM customers c
INNER JOIN (
  -- TODO: grouped + HAVING subquery
) oc ON c.customer_id = oc.customer_id
ORDER BY oc.total_orders DESC;
